title: How his melodies come to him
summary: He started writing numbers around 20; since he cannot write notation, he tapes tunes that come in his sleep.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When did you start writing your numbers?
Well, numbers, I got that big way. I got those things right there when I got that.
Been at 20 years old. Some ideas came to me, and they still come to me.
Ideas about numbers come to me. I can't write, though. But they come to me, and how I did to capture those few air, because during the time when I'd be sleeping, and they come.
Yeah, all right. Dave Williams, second reel. How about going? You were talking about those melodies, how they'd come to you.

Oh, yeah, they'd come to me, you know. While I'm laying back sleeping, different little melodies come to me. So I did to capture the little things I had there. At the time, I had a tape record, and I'd get up. I was my best out in writing, because I, you know, I'd not say writing, but my best way of getting my numbers, because I couldn't write. So I'd get up, and I'd tape them right fast, and I have them. But if they come to me, and I fool around there, say, well, I'll wait till I get up in the morning, and see what they're saying, you know. Well, it'd be they go away from me. I mean, I have things come to me now. But I've been kind of late on the job. It seemed like I wasn't going to never make a success in this thing, so. I just don't play melodies in the mind anymore. I just play all the melodies I hear from other people. But, it seems like things changing now, in this music world for me. I'm doing better now with it than what I ever did so far, so. I guess anything that come my way, you understand that I, you know, I'll be on the ball for it now.
